label: late original-phase "d" after t/r/3/y context
explanation: Very sparse feature (about 0.002% of steps). About 92% of activation mass is on input "d" during the original phase at positions 5-7 (orig_idx 4-8), mostly near the end of the original sequence (to_go 0-2). It does not fire in the copy phase; 2 weak activations fall on <DEL>. Most "d"s do not trigger it: whether it fires depends on earlier context. Activations are larger when the prefix contains several of t, r, 3, y (often first token y, t in position 1, r/3 later). Predicting d plus at least 3 of those tokens seen catches about 75% of mass at only ~7% precision, and requiring 4 raises precision to ~20% but drops recall. The rule for which prefix tokens matter is not fully captured.
